allow.src/art/mockup-reference.ts#MOCKUP_GROUN: SURFACE — the design's own ground hex, and its whole job is to be COMPARED with production rather than called by it (a0-40). `backdrop.test.ts` asserts `FLOOR === MOCKUP_GROUND`; a version of this that production imported could not fail that assertion, which is the one thing it is for. The gate this file installs exists because for six developer reports nothing in CI compared the backdrop to its design. See §4.6.
allow.src/art/mockup-reference.ts#MOCKUP_SKY_I: SURFACE — the design's own index of the five skies with geometry, so the gate iterates the DESIGN's list rather than the backdrop's `NEBULA_IDS` (a0-40). Iterating production's list would make a sky that vanished from the registry pass by not being looked at. See §4.6.
allow.src/art/mockup-reference.ts#STAR_TEMPERA: SURFACE — the allow-list's own oracle (a0-45). A star's colour is a CONTINUOUS function of its temperature (`starColorFor`), so the design's star hues are the one thing in the art that cannot be a member of `ALLOWED_COLORS`; this is that function enumerated over the design's own domain, and `compliance.ts` — itself SURFACE, a linter run by specs — is what reads it. Production paints `starColorFor(temp)` directly, which it must: the set exists so a hand-edited star hex still fails the audit. Same shape as haloRadiusOf. See §4.6.
allow.src/art/mockup-reference.ts#haloKneeAlph: SURFACE — the design's own bloom RULE, exported so the design's DATA can be asserted against something that is not itself (a0-44). `MOCKUP_STARS.bloom.radius` and `spike.length` shipped wrong for a release while a test asserted each equalled the constant someone had typed; `backdrop.test.ts` now asserts `radius === haloRadiusOf(intensity)` and its three neighbours, so a typist cannot satisfy the gate. Production reads the VALUES — it must, they are the design's committed numbers — and CI reads the rules that produce them. Same shape as MOCKUP_GROUND. See §4.6.

See docs/dark-matter-scan.md §4.9.

allow.src/ui/font-boot.ts#awaitRatifiedFaces: SURFACE — an entry point's own front door, and its CALLER IS HTML (§6). index.html's inline entry script imports this and awaits it before it dynamically imports src/main.ts, so it runs on every boot of every build (u14-01, GDD §5.6): it is what blocks first paint until Audiowide and Oxanium have loaded, because Pixi bakes canvas text into a texture that is never redrawn. A TypeScript reachability scan cannot read that caller. The module is listed in DEFAULT_ENTRIES so everything BEYOND the door — RATIFIED_FACES, BOOT_FONT_DEADLINE_MS — resolves live; only the handle itself is unreachable, which is what a door is. Do not delete: deleting it makes the first painted frame a coin flip between two typefaces and every golden in the suite non-reproducible.
